title: rfc-9596 COSE "typ" (type) header parameter (derived)
description: DERIVED - not verbatim. RFC 9596 ships no grammar of any kind (CDDL, ABNF, ASN.1 and JSON Schema each occur zero times in it). This is the library's fixture-validation rendering over a JSON projection in which an integer COSE label appears as the decimal string of that integer. THE PROJECTION IS OURS. The CDDL in this directory is the authority on the CBOR.

oneOf.title: an unsigned integer registered in the CoAP Content-Formats registry
a string content type value: a media type name, optionally with media type parameters (§2, MAY, unconstrained)

x-library-notes.optional: §2: 'Use of this header parameter is OPTIONAL.' There is no required property here, and nothing in RFC 9596, rfc-9597 or rfc-9942 ever requires typ.
x-library-notes.placement: §2's only obligation - 'The "typ" parameter MUST NOT be present in unprotected headers' - is UNENFORCEABLE in a JSON projection, which has no protected/unprotected distinction. It lives in the CDDL and in requirements.yaml R-0015.
x-library-notes.equality: NOT EXPRESSIBLE AND LOAD-BEARING. typ 61 and 'application/cwt' denote the same type (rfc-8392 §9.3.1 and §9.2.1) and compare unequal. Media type names are case-insensitive and a CBOR tstr is not, and §2 permits media type parameters unconstrained. A confusion-resistance mechanism with an unspecified equality relation can be defeated by respelling the type.
x-library-notes.no-check: §2 tells COSE libraries to ignore this parameter and §3's two reject rules are lower case, so a conformant implementation performs no check. A schema cannot supply the obligation the specification declines to state.
